summary: Bosentan is a dual endothelin (ETA and ETB) receptor antagonist used to treat pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) to improve exercise capacity and slow clinical worsening. It carries a BOXED WARNING for hepatotoxicity (requiring monthly liver enzyme testing) and for serious birth defects (teratogenicity), so it is available only through a restricted REMS programme with mandatory pregnancy testing and reliable contraception. It also reduces hemoglobin and is a strong inducer of CYP3A4/CYP2C9 with important drug interactions.
indications: Treatment of pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH, WHO Group 1) to improve exercise ability and decrease clinical worsening
In systemic sclerosis with ongoing digital ulcer disease, to reduce the number of new digital ulcers (where approved)

dosage.n: After 4 weeks; this is the usual target dose

dosage.d: If already on ritonavir >=10 days: start bosentan 62.5 mg once daily or every other day
Contraindicated in moderate to severe impairment
dosage.n: Avoid; mild impairment use with caution

admin: Take in the morning and evening, with or without food
Swallow tablets; dispersible tablets may be dispersed in water for those unable to swallow
Do not start without baseline liver enzymes and a negative pregnancy test
Obtain monthly liver function tests and monthly pregnancy tests throughout treatment
Dispensed only through the restricted REMS access programme
moa: Endothelin-1 is a potent vasoconstrictor and smooth-muscle mitogen acting on ETA and ETB receptors, and is elevated in pulmonary arterial hypertension. Bosentan competitively antagonises both ETA and ETB receptors, producing pulmonary (and systemic) vasodilation and reducing vascular proliferation, thereby lowering pulmonary vascular resistance and improving exercise capacity.

absolute: Moderate to severe hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh B/C) or baseline aminotransferases >3x ULN
relative: Concomitant strong CYP3A4 inducers/inhibitors or hormonal contraceptives (reduced contraceptive efficacy)
monitor: Pregnancy test - monthly in women of childbearing potential
Hemoglobin/hematocrit - at 1 and 3 months then every 3 months

preg: CONTRAINDICATED (boxed warning). Bosentan is teratogenic and causes serious birth defects. Pregnancy must be excluded before starting, prevented with two reliable methods of contraception during and for one month after, and tested for monthly. Hormonal contraceptives alone are not reliable because bosentan induces their metabolism.
lact: It is not known whether bosentan is excreted in human milk. Because of the potential for serious adverse reactions, breastfeeding is not recommended during treatment.
renal: No dose adjustment is required in renal impairment, and bosentan is not removed by dialysis. Renal clearance contributes little to elimination.
hepatic: BOXED WARNING for hepatotoxicity. Bosentan causes dose-dependent elevations of liver aminotransferases and rare liver injury. It is contraindicated in moderate-to-severe hepatic impairment and if baseline ALT/AST exceed 3x ULN. Measure aminotransferases before treatment and monthly thereafter; reduce, interrupt or stop per the elevation and any symptoms of hepatic injury.

major: Cyclosporine A (contraindicated - markedly raises bosentan, lowers cyclosporine)
Glyburide (contraindicated - increased hepatotoxicity, reduced hypoglycemic effect)
Hormonal contraceptives (bosentan induces metabolism - may fail; use additional non-hormonal method)
Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors + CYP2C9 inhibitors together (avoid - raise bosentan markedly)
Ritonavir and other CYP3A4 inhibitors (dose-adjust bosentan)
moderate: Statins metabolised by CYP3A4 e.g. simvastatin, atorvastatin (reduced levels - monitor lipids)
interactions.food: May be taken with or without food; no significant food effect
interactions.alcohol: Avoid excessive alcohol due to additive hepatotoxic potential
interactions.diagnostics: Elevates serum aminotransferases; may lower hemoglobin/hematocrit

serious: Hepatotoxicity (elevated transaminases, hepatitis, rare liver failure)
Significant decrease in hemoglobin requiring transfusion
Fluid retention and worsening heart failure
emergency: Acute liver failure (jaundice, dark urine, severe RUQ pain)

monitoring: Monthly pregnancy test in women of childbearing potential
Hemoglobin at 1 and 3 months, then quarterly
Signs of fluid retention / heart failure
counsel: This drug can seriously harm a developing baby - you must use two reliable forms of contraception and have monthly pregnancy tests
Hormonal contraceptives (pill, patch, implant) may not work - use an additional barrier method
Attend monthly blood tests for your liver
Report yellowing of skin/eyes, dark urine, nausea, unusual tiredness, or abdominal pain at once
Do not stop the medicine abruptly without medical advice
pk: Steady-state plasma levels reached in about 3-5 days
Plasma peak approximately 3-5 hours after oral dose
Store at 20-25 C, protected from moisture
pearls: BOXED WARNINGS: hepatotoxicity (monthly LFTs) and teratogenicity (REMS, monthly pregnancy tests, dual contraception)
Bosentan induces CYP3A4 and CYP2C9, reducing efficacy of hormonal contraceptives, warfarin and many statins
Cyclosporine A and glyburide are absolutely contraindicated co-medications
Expect a fall in hemoglobin - monitor and investigate significant drops
Available only through a restricted distribution / REMS programme
missed: Take the missed dose as soon as you remember unless it is almost time for the next dose, in which case skip it and resume your usual twice-daily schedule. Do not double the dose. Do not stop the medicine on your own.
overdose: Experience is limited; very high single doses in healthy volunteers caused headache, nausea and vomiting. Massive overdose may cause marked hypotension requiring cardiovascular support. There is no specific antidote - provide supportive intensive care; dialysis is not expected to be useful given high protein binding.
